import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Dickson's conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture)
- [PrimePages glossary](https://t5k.org/glossary/xpage/DicksonsConjecture.html)
- [OEIS Wiki](https://oeis.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture)
- [MathWorld](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/DicksonsConjecture.html)
- [Leonard Eugene Dickson, *History of the Theory of Numbers, Vol. I: Divisibility and Primality*](https://archive.org/details/historyoftheoryo01dickuoft)
- [Arxiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.3850)
-/
open Polynomial
namespace Dickson

/--
**Dickson's conjecture**
If a finite set of linear integer forms $f_i(n) = a_i n+b_i$ satisfies Schinzel condition,
there exist infinitely many natural numbers $m$ such that $f_i(m)$ are primes for all $i$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem dickson_conjecture (fs : Finset ℤ[X]) (hfs : ∀ f ∈ fs, f.degree = 1 ∧ BunyakovskyCondition f)
    (hfs' : SchinzelCondition fs) : Infinite {n : ℕ | ∀ f ∈ fs, (f.eval (n : ℤ)).natAbs.Prime} := by
  sorry

/-  ## Special cases -/

/--
**The generalized twin-prime conjecture**
For any positive integer $k$ there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p + 2k$ is prime.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem generalized_twin_primes (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) :
    Infinite {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ (p + 2 * k).Prime} := by
  sorry

/--
**The infinitude of Sophie Germain primes**
There are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $2p + 1$ is prime.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinite_safe_primes :
    Infinite {p : ℕ | Prime p ∧ Prime (2 * p + 1)} := by
  sorry

/--
**The infinitude of cousin primes**
There are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p + 4$ is prime.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinite_cousin_primes :
    Infinite {p : ℕ | Prime p ∧ Prime (p + 4)} := by
  sorry

/--
**The infinitude of sexy primes**
There are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p + 6$ is prime.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinite_sexy_primes :
    Infinite {p : ℕ | Prime p ∧ Prime (p + 6)} := by
  sorry

/-
## Other consequences
- Landau's fourth problem (primes and perfect squares)
- Twin prime conjecture
- Artin's primitive root conjecture
- First Hardy–Littlewood conjecture

*Reference:* [Arxiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.3850)
-/

end Dickson

findings.description: The docstring at lines 35–36 mentions only the Schinzel condition and omits positivity of the coefficients a_i. The Lean statement correctly requires positive leading coefficients through BunyakovskyCondition. With the source's convention that primes are positive, the prose alone is false: the singleton {-X} satisfies SchinzelCondition but has no positive prime values on ℕ. This is a documentation issue, not a defect in the theorem statement.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia's opening statement requires each slope b_i ≥ 1: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture. Zhang, Notes on Dickson's Conjecture, arXiv:0906.3850v3, Introduction, likewise explicitly assumes b_i ≥ 1 in f_i(x)=a_i+b_i x.
findings.suggested_fix: Add “with a_i > 0” to the docstring's description of f_i(n)=a_i n+b_i. No Lean statement change is needed.

findings.description: The prose-only “Other consequences” list at lines 82–88 incorrectly attributes Landau's fourth problem to the linear-forms Dickson conjecture. The cited paper instead discusses the quadratic polynomial x²+1 under Bunyakovsky's conjecture; it does not include Landau's fourth problem in its list of Dickson consequences. No Lean declaration encodes this erroneous attribution.
findings.source_evidence: Zhang, arXiv:0906.3850v3, Introduction, identifies x²+1 as the simplest still-open Bunyakovsky case before separately introducing Dickson's linear conjecture. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landau%27s_problems, “Near-square primes,” identifies the fourth problem as infinitude of primes n²+1 and lists Bunyakovsky and Bateman–Horn as conjectures implying it. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schinzel%27s_hypothesis_H, “Examples,” gives x²+1 as an instance of hypothesis H.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the Landau bullet from this list, or explicitly attribute it to generalized Dickson's conjecture (Schinzel's hypothesis H), rather than the linear conjecture formalized here.

reformulations.difference: The Lean formulation adds irreducibility through BunyakovskyCondition, uses natural-number witnesses for admissibility, tests primality of absolute values, and allows the empty finite family. The source uses positive-slope linear forms, no fixed integer divisor greater than one of all product values, and infinitely many positive inputs with positive prime values.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a degree-one integer polynomial aX+b, admissibility rules out a common prime divisor of a and b, hence implies irreducibility; that additional hypothesis is redundant. A prime divides a finite product exactly when it divides a factor, and every integer greater than one has a prime divisor. An integer witness modulo a prime can be replaced by its nonnegative residue, preserving all polynomial divisibility tests. Positive integer slopes make every polynomial value positive once n exceeds the maximum absolute constant coefficient, so absolute-value primality and positive-prime values differ only on a finite prefix; including n=0 does not affect infinitude. The empty family contributes only a provable trivial case. The full universal equivalence is proved as dickson_formulation_equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using the file's sorry theorems.

reformulations.difference: The declaration counts Sophie Germain primes p rather than the associated safe primes q=2p+1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The map p ↦ 2p+1 is a bijection from Sophie Germain primes onto safe primes, so the two sets are infinite simultaneously. On ℕ, the generic Prime predicate is equivalent to Nat.Prime. This equivalence is proved as sophie_infinitude_iff_safe in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: All five Lean theorem statements are faithful; the findings concern prose only. The generalized-twin statement correctly asks for arbitrary prime pairs, not necessarily consecutive primes. All five research-open tags agree with the consulted sources. Scratch checks covered the empty family, zero and constant polynomials, admissible {X}, inadmissible {X, X+1}, sign conventions, and small instances of all prime-pair predicates. The scratch file compiles without errors or warnings; the equivalence proofs have no sorryAx dependency. The cited OEIS Wiki returned HTTP 403 and MathWorld HTTP 404. The cited Internet Archive identifier also returned 404, but the same volume was located and read under historyoftheoryo01dick. These access problems did not prevent verification of any declaration.
